title: Architecture Decision Record Primitive
description: Records a non-obvious, hard-to-reverse architectural decision. Follows the Nygard template. Stored in docs/adr/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md.

context.description: What problem are we solving? What constraints exist? What forces are at play?

decision.description: What we decided. One sentence summary followed by rationale.

rejectedBecause.description: Why this alternative was not chosen.

alternatives.description: At least one alternative must be listed. An ADR with no alternatives is not an ADR.

consequences.description: What becomes easier, what becomes harder. Both must be non-empty.

creationCriteria.description: An ADR is warranted when a decision meets ANY of:
criteria: Hard to reverse (database schema, API contract, file format, protocol)
Surprising without context (a reader would ask 'why did they do it this way?')
Real trade-off (two plausible alternatives, each with meaningful consequences)
antiCriteria: Obvious choices ('use Postgres because we already use Postgres')
Easily reversible ('start with a flat JSON file and migrate later')

storageTarget.format: Markdown with frontmatter or heading-structured sections matching the schema

crossReference.description: When an ADR bears on a glossary term, add 'see ADR #N' to the term's adrReferences in CONTEXT.md.
